R764.note: Converts GET to POST + existing CrossOriginProtection middleware, matching sibling routes - a valid approach; but silently breaks the stated design that the deletion link is clickable directly from an email (a bare <a href> cannot issue POST), and the write-up never flags that callers/UI need to change.

R765.note: Overflow check is sound, but the 'Fixed code' keeps `return buffer;` where buffer is now std::vector<uint8_t> while never updating the function's declared `uint8_t*` return type shown in the file - as presented this will not compile. The ownership/type change is only loosely mentioned in prose, not reconciled with a working signature.

R766.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the right annotation, but it's placed in a brand-new class in an unrelated package (com.example.config) instead of the already-scanned sibling SecurityConfig.java in com.example.accounts, risking it never being component-scanned; if it does take effect there is no other behavior change.

R767.note: Overflow check is correct and non-overflowing itself; vector is used as a safe intermediate and then copied into a new[]-allocated buffer matching the original raw-pointer return signature/ownership contract exactly.
